subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory CRUD write contract to memory-core, and what hard-limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The source-level capability gap is clear, but implementing it creates new public memory-write, persistence, config, and security behavior that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
options.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, and secret policy before code lands.

options.title: Narrow to existing paths
options.body: Keep first-class CRUD out of memory-core for now and address bloat through existing memory-flush, promotion, recall, and diagnostics surfaces.

options.title: Prototype as external memory plugin
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype the write policy as a memory plugin or ClawHub package until a core or plugin API gap is proven.

recommendation.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
recommendation.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, and secret policy before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for memory-core ownership and the remaining product/API direction points to steipete.
